zotero.abstractNote: Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) models have demonstrated remarkable zero-shot performance on various downstream tasks. However, the extent to which these models rely on compositional reasoning versus simple feature matching remains a subject of debate. In this work, we investigate the internal representations of CLIP by analyzing its sensitivity to word order. We find that CLIP behaves like a bag-of-words model in its cross-modal alignment, where the order of words in a prompt has minimal impact on the image-text similarity score. Conversely, we show that the uni-modal text encoder of CLIP retains significant sensitivity to word order, suggesting that the bag-of-words behavior is an emergent property of the cross-modal contrastive objective rather than a limitation of the text encoder itself. We provide extensive empirical evidence across multiple datasets and model architectures to support our findings.
